subject: Referring to the common factor mean (alpha) within the model definition

messages.author: 73fb61795976b321
messages.subject: Referring to the common factor mean (alpha) within the model definition
parts:
Hello all,

Is there a simple way to refer to the mean of the common factor within the model definition? I know i can get the estimated values using lavInspect as below, but I would like to give it a name. Is that possible?

lavInspect(mod.fit,what = "est")$alpha  

For example, in the following model, I can easily refer to the common factor variance as var. Can I do the same for the mean?   Would eta ~ mean*1 do the trick?

mod <- ' eta =~ A + B + C

eta~~var*eta
' 

Looking forward to hearing from you,

Hugo

messages.subject: Re: Referring to the common factor mean (alpha) within the model definition
parts:

eta~1

You can name it as
eta~MN*1

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: Referring to the common factor mean (alpha) within the model definition
parts:
Hugo,

Your first question was about giving the mean a name. By default, as you indicate here, the mean is constrained to 0 for identification. Giving it a name would be meaningless, since it's a constant.

But specifying eta ~ 1, with or without a name, frees the mean.

As for "are the models different," I suggest you run both of them and see. That will give you a better intuition for the future about what's going on than my answer will.

Pat
